extracted.intended_audience: chemists, metallurgists, instrument-makers, and scientific Fellows of the Royal Society
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed experimental protocol and practical recommendations for converting crude platinum ore into malleable, workable platinum (with accompanying procedures for palladium and osmium oxide), aimed at practitioners performing laboratory-scale metallurgy and instrument construction. Includes also a separate set of practical design criteria for a microscopic doublet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilution of muriatic acid
rubrics_metrics.description: To every measure of the strongest muriatic acid employed, there be added an equal measure of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended to avoid dissolving iridium contained in the ore; stated as a precaution the author had omitted previously. Purpose: obtain chemical purity and avoid extracting iridium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type/strength of nitric acid
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'single aquafortis' (i.e. ordinary nitric acid), not stronger varieties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advised both for obtaining a purer result and economy in purchasing nitric acid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proportions of nitro-muriatic menstruum
rubrics_metrics.description: Rough proportions given: muriatic acid equivalent to 150 marble together with nitric acid equivalent to 40 marble will take 100 of crude platina; include at least 20% redundancy of ore in the menstruum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given in 'round numbers' to avoid waste of acid and render solution purer; these are practical working proportions rather than precise stoichiometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digestion time and heating of acids
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow the acids to digest three or four days with a heat which ought to be gradually raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long digestion and gradual heating recommended to ensure dissolution without unnecessarily aggressive conditions that might dissolve undesirable constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settling/decanting before precipitation
rubrics_metrics.description: After pouring off the solution, let it stand until fine pulverulent ore of iridium suspended in the liquid has completely subsided before further processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: remove suspended iridium prior to precipitation with sal ammoniac to avoid incorporating iridium into the platinum precipitate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precipitation with sal ammoniac — proportions and washing
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix solution with 41 parts of sal ammoniac dissolved in about five times their weight of water to obtain the first precipitate (example yields given: ~165 parts precipitate yielding ~66 parts pure platinum). Wash the yellow precipitate well and press to remove washings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thorough washing is essential to free the precipitate from other impurities present in the complex ore; pressing removes remnants of washings before further thermal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recovery of platinum from mother-liquor
rubrics_metrics.description: Mother-liquor still contains platinum; recover by precipitation with clean iron bars (cementation), redissolve the precipitate in appropriate aqua regia and treat further.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recover residual platinum and other metals; later adjust acid proportions before final sal-ammoniac precipitation to avoid coprecipitation of palladium or lead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acid adjustment to avoid co-precipitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before adding sal ammoniac to a re-dissolved precipitate, mix about 1 part by measure of strong muriatic acid with 32 parts of the nitro-muriatic solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents precipitation of palladium or lead along with the ammonio-muriate of platina — an explicit anti-pattern mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thermal decomposition of ammonio-muriate: low, cautious heating
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat the yellow precipitate with the utmost caution in a black-lead pot, with so low a heat as just to expel the whole of the sal ammoniac, and to occasion the particles of platina to cohere as little as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objective: avoid over-heating which increases cohesion and harms later welding/ductility; overheating is explicitly warned against as damaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid burnishing during grinding
rubrics_metrics.description: Grind coarser parts in a wooden bowl with a wooden pestle; on no account use any harder material capable of burnishing the particles of platina.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every degree of burnishing will prevent the particles from cohering in later stages; author gives an experiment showing burnished surfaces weld with difficulty — explicit anti-pattern: burnishing destroys welding ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce extremely fine metallic powder by gentle means
rubrics_metrics.description: Lightly coherent grey product should be rubbed between the hands to procure as much metallic powder as possible fine enough to pass through a fine lawn sieve; coarser parts then ground in wood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gentlest means preferred to avoid burnishing; use water in later grinding to suspend and remove fine portions as they are reduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purification by mechanical diffusion through water
rubrics_metrics.description: Since platinum cannot be fused for purification, mechanical diffusion through water (repeated washing, shaking, and decanting) should be used to allow earthy matters to come to the surface and to make water effect the purifying powers of fluxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author frames this as the analogue of melting/flux purification for metals that cannot be fused in ordinary furnaces; repeated washing yields fine gray powder as pure as other metals are by ordinary metallurgy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of a uniform 'mud' for casting
rubrics_metrics.description: Pour purified platinum powder over and allow to subside in a clean basin to obtain a uniform mud or pulp ready for casting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure uniformity to avoid cavities in the pressed ingot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mould design and filling procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a brass barrel turned slightly taper inside (dimensions given) plugged at larger extremity with a steel stopper that enters a quarter inch; grease inside with a little lard; surround stopper with blotting-paper; set barrel upright in a jug of water and fill the barrel with the platinum mud while submerged so it fills without cavities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tapered interior, blotting-paper to facilitate escape of water, filling in water to avoid air pockets; weigh barrel after filling to check for cavities by comparing against expected weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weight-checking to detect cavities
rubrics_metrics.description: Weigh the barrel after filling and compare the actual weight of its contents with the estimated weight it ought to contain; a materially lower weight indicates lack of uniformity (cavities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author gives calculation example for expected weight; this is an explicit quality control/check step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-compression preparation to allow water escape
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay a circular piece of soft paper then woollen cloth upon the surface to allow water to pass during partial compression by hand with a wooden plug; place a circular copper plate on top before laying horizontally in a forcible press.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These layers facilitate controlled water escape and permit the barrel contents to gain enough consistency to be handled and compressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression: press usage and carry to limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Compress in a strong press (design described) and carry compression to 'the utmost limit possible'; then extract cake and heat on charcoal to drive off moisture and grease and give firmer cohesion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author describes mechanical advantage of the press and insists on maximal practical compression prior to thermal treatment; over-compression is not warned against but maximal achievable is advised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wind-furnace heating to prevent blistering
rubrics_metrics.description: Heat the cake in a wind-furnace on an earthen stand strown with clean quartzose sand, place cake upright, cover with inverted refractory cylindrical pot not touching the cake; feed the furnace with Staffordshire coke and continue action for about twenty minutes with a breathing heat during last 4–5 minutes — intense heat needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose to the most intense heat possible to drive off residual impurities that lower temperatures might render volatile; objective is to prevent blistering during subsequent work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forging technique for closing and shaping ingot
rubrics_metrics.description: After furnace heating, while the cake is hot place upright on an anvil and strike on the top with a heavy hammer so as in one heating to close the metal; if cylinder becomes bent, do not hammer the side (which would crack irremediably) but straighten by blows on the extremities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct forging blows and avoiding side hammering are explicitly specified to prevent irreversible cracking; after this the ingot may be reduced by heating and forging like other metals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleaning forged ingot from ferruginous scales
rubrics_metrics.description: Smear surface with moistened mixture of equal parts by measure of crystallized borax and common salt of tartar, fuse, then expose on a platinum tray under an inverted pot to wind-furnace heat; afterwards plunge into dilute sulphuric acid to dissolve the flux.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flux dissolves ferruginous scales acquired in fire; dilute sulphuric acid removes flux residues; author suggests an alternate flux composition in a footnote for mineral analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation metrics for success — specific gravity and tenacity
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimate perfection by comparing specific gravity of prepared platinum with platinum that has undergone complete fusion (values given: 21.16–21.5) and by measuring tenacity (weights to break wires) with examples and comparative values vs gold and iron.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author gives measured tenacity ranges and suggests 590 pounds (from 11 trials) as measure for prepared platinum; concrete empirical benchmarks are provided for quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Palladium: sulphur-route and patient roast/tap processing
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain malleable palladium, combine the residuum from burning the prussiate with sulphur, fuse, purify by cupellation with borax and nitre, roast the sulphuret at low red heat until spongy, press to flat cake, roast patiently at low red heat alternating with light hammer tappings until cake bears heavier blows and can be passed through rolling/flattening mills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author notes the process yields palladium always brittle when hot (probably retains some sulphur); he prefers this sulphur method to fusion-per-se which produces hard, difficult-to-manage product.

rubrics_metrics.name: Osmium oxide isolation by nitre treatment and rapid distillation
rubrics_metrics.description: Grind 3 parts pulverulent ore of iridium with 1 part nitre in cold crucible, heat to red until pasty and osmic fumes arise; dissolve soluble parts in minimal water, mix with sulphuric acid diluted with its weight of water equivalent to potash in nitre, then distil rapidly to collect osmic oxide as a white crust which melts into drops and crystallizes on cooling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author gives operation details and yields (example yielded 30 grains crystallized oxide plus strong aqueous solution); rapid distillation while fumes continue is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscope illumination principle
rubrics_metrics.description: In illumination of microscopic objects, light collected and brought to the eye beyond that fully commanded by the object-glasses tends to impede rather than assist distinct vision; collect as much admitted light as can be done by simple means to a focus in the same plane as the object.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical advice: use a plane mirror to direct the light and a plano-convex lens to collect it with the plane side towards the object; avoid extraneous light outside the object-glass control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lens form and orientation for microscope (plano-convex preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer a plano-convex lens with its plane side next to the object; sapphire plano-convex lenses have decided superiority, but glass plano-convex used appropriately is very good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author prefers simple single lenses for extreme distinctness when examining unknown minute bodies; gives practical advantage that if a plano-convex lens touches a fluid under examination view is not impaired but often improved; contrasts with double-convex where touching fluid spoils examination until lens is wiped.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compound magnifier (doublet) configuration and spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Use two plano-convex lenses arranged like two thimbles screwed together with plane sides toward the object; proportion of foci near 3:1; joint performance best when distance between their plane surfaces is about 1/40 of the shorter focus (author's empirical proportions—distance to be varied by trial).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spacing should be varied by experiment until greatest distinctness across the whole field is achieved; author describes a simple adjustable cell method using pieces of plane glass and a spring to measure inter-surface distance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tube/internal baffling and dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a tube about six inches long of diameter sufficient to preclude reflexion from its sides; blacken the inside to prevent stray reflections; place plano-convex collecting lens near the top (plane side toward object); include a circular perforation (about 0.3 inch) near the bottom to limit light.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Length (~6 inches) chosen for comfortable eye height; diameter and interior blackening prevent false light; image of perforation should be small (~1/20 inch for intended powers) and its plane brought to same plane as object by adjustable distance between lens and perforation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment and adjustment for best field performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Axes of lenses and center of perforation must be in the same right line; ensure the image of the perforation is illuminated throughout with uniformly defined circumference; provide means to vary distance between illuminating lens and perforation and adjustable stage for lateral adjustments; focus adjustment applied to compound magnifier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author emphasizes full-field distinctness (not only center) and suggests mechanical arrangements (screwing tubes, flanged exterior cell) to allow easy changes and fine adjustment; bull's-eye lantern recommended for night illumination.
